title: Review test workflow
body:
- Run linting only once
- Update actions/cache to v4
- Run e2e-tests with <del>the same matrix as the others</del> node 18 instead of node 16
- Change cache keys to avoid cache collisions
author: KristjanESPERANTO

comments.body: Thanks, looks reasonable. But I don't think we should run the e2e tests multiple times, since they go against the live DB APIs (and as happening in this run, they are quite unstable, although that's maybe only due to my change of the HAFAS journeys IDs/refreshCtx where the departure times seem to toggle (?)). But probably it makes sense to run them on a newer node version :)

> But I don't think we should run the e2e tests multiple times, since they go against the live DB APIs

Okay, that's a good point against my change. I've just changed it back to run only once.

> But probably it makes sense to run them on a newer node version :)

Yeah, I changed it to node 18, which is the oldest node version that hasn't reached End Of Life yet.
Thanks, I guess this didn't occur to me as sufficiently important yet :)

title: Use risZuglaufId to get fahrtNr
body:
fahrtNr is currently unreliable. For hafas-client it was always interpretable as int, currently it is not. For example, for the following line it does not return the correct result (`6` instead of the correct `31600`)

```
{
  administrationId: "8003S_",
  risZuglaufId: "S_31600",
  risAbfahrtId: "8003368_2025-01-10T17:21:00+01:00",
  kurztext: "S",
  mitteltext: "S 6",
  langtext: "S 6",
  zuglaufId: "2|#VN#1#ST#1736364871#PI#1#ZI#212722#TA#5#DA#100125#1S#8004948#1T#1614#LS#8003373#LT#1746#PU#81#RT#1#CA#s#ZE#6#ZB#S      6#PC#4#FR#8004948#FT#1614#TO#8003373#TT#1746#",
  nummer: 4,
  typ: "FAHRZEUG",
  abgangsDatum: "2025-01-10T17:21:00+01:00",
  ankunftsDatum: "2025-01-10T17:23:00+01:00",
  verkehrsmittelNummer: "6",
  richtung: "Köln-Worringen",
  produktGattung: "SBAHN",
  wagenreihung: true,
  ...
}
```

For dbnav, the correct `fahrtNr` always seems to be included in the `risZuglaufId`
author: McToel

comments.body:
Yes, `line.fahrtNr` and `line.id` are terrible, although I would have thought that for dbnav `verkehrsmittelNummer` is reliable, but apparently for S-Bahns it does not contain the actual train number. So thanks! Maybe we should also incorporate `risZuglaufId` into `line.id` then, what do you think?
And we should probably add a test (maybe a fixture `dbnav-journeys`, since that doesn't exist yet,  or easier a unit test in `parse/line.js`), since nothing turned red :D But I can also do that later if you want.
As discussed in #9, additionally including `zugName` here may be useful in some cases, where `fahrtNr` would remain unset otherwise
Yes, if nobody is working on this rn, I'll just merge this PR as is and add the rest discussed here and in #9.

Done. Note that the correct `fahrtNr` is only contained for journeys, not for trips and boards in the dbnav profile, and mostly only for boards in the db profile. Additionally, this varies according to product...

2535bb6 also removed the new unit test, which tested the `formatJourneysReq()` function of the db profile.
For re-adding a unit test for this pr, would you prefer the test to sit in its own file or should I just add it to `tests/db-journey.js`?

Yes sad to see the unit test go, it also tested the 0/null thing :) (although I'm confused, was it ever green? or why did the `null` -> `undefined` work :thinking: ) 
Keep it where you prefer, although for the -1 thing it will probably be difficult to test with a unit test now that you've moved it to index.js?

It did in fact pass, but by mistake 😅
`same()` apparently allows conversion between `null` and `undefined`. I should have used `equal()` instead, where the test does not pass. Oh well...
I could maybe add a second fixture where `transfers` is set to zero and then check for the correct result for different `transfers` values. What do you think?

Ah good to know, but yeah now that I remember that in fact `null == undefined`, no wonder. And, well, `same()` is used throughout the codebase, so that's normal :)
Fixture, you mean in the e2e tests? The problem with these is that in CI they are also run against the live APIs, so we don't want too many requests. Or you meant introducing unit test fixtures for requests? That might be possible. I would probably just leave this untested tbh and just keep the null/0 unit test or move the -1 back into the journey-reqs again :see_no_evil: Do it however you see fit :)

I think all in all, the best solution may even be to move this to a new file `format/journeys-req.js`, where option modifications concerning all profiles would live. This would allow for easy testing on the one hand and prevent code duplication on the other hand, so we'd kind of have the best of both worlds here. This would also ensure similar changes won't bloat `index.js` in the future

EDIT: nevermind, the other "-req" files in `format` work differently (they return the "db format" directly), so that would probably make the whole thing more confusing. I think, I'll stick with the solution of adding the changes to the `journeys-req.js` files in the profile directories 😅

If the potential next profile doesn't actually require transfers to be set to -1 :D These DB APIs are always great for surprises. And I have removed the hooking logic used in hafas-client for stacking transforms/formats. So not sure how exactly one would then elegantly call the individual profile-specific journey-reqs from there. Maybe one could just introduce a `profile.formatTransfers` function that can be called from the two journey-reqs?
That sounds like a good idea, I'll do that
I *think* this is it (finally)
wait, forgot removing prior changes to index.js
Cool :) Thanks a lot!
Thanks for the detailed feedback, genuinely improved my understanding of the codebase ^^

title: results option is being ignored by journeys function
body:
## expected:

when calling the `journeys` function with the `results: 1` option, I expected the max number of results to be 1.

## actual:

```
 let data = await client.journeys(berlinJungfernheide, münchenHbf, {
        results: 1,
        tickets: true,
 })
```

returns more than one journey:

```
{
  earlierRef: '3|OB|MTµ14µ541001µ541001µ541272µ541272µ0µ0µ485µ540980µ1µ0µ26µ0µ0µ-2147483648µ1µ2|PDHµ5cad74a0d15ed317fb4ba0dde7ed8b36|RDµ17122024|RTµ162300|USµ0|RSµINIT',
  laterRef: '3|OF|MTµ14µ541180µ541180µ541441µ541441µ0µ0µ485µ541122µ5µ0µ26µ0µ0µ-2147483648µ1µ2|PDHµ5cad74a0d15ed317fb4ba0dde7ed8b36|RDµ17122024|RTµ162300|USµ0|RSµINIT',
  journeys: [
    [Object], [Object],
    [Object], [Object],
    [Object], [Object],
    [Object]
  ],
  realtimeDataUpdatedAt: null
}
```
author: grssnbchr

comments.body:
Yes, the new backend API does unfortunately not allow specifying the number of desired results. There are quite a few parameters like that that are not known to exist in the new API or I that was too lazy to implement so far (see `TODO`s scattered across the code).
The journey list is now truncated if `results` is set, however, you will not be able to increase the number of returned results (use `laterThan` with additional requests for that).
Got it, thanks!
